title: Per-request variability mitigation workbook
summary: Workbook exploring how per-request variability (sequence length, short bursts, tail latencies) inflates hosted API unit economics and operational mitigations (micro-caching, adaptive batching, reserve pools). Includes regional PPK mocks, scenario slices, and recommended actions for the roadmap.
content:
OVERVIEW:
This sheet models the cost uplift caused by request-level variability (short vs long sequences, bursty arrival patterns, and tail latency penalties) for hosted-api traffic. Goal: produce actionable mitigations that reduce observed PPK and stabilize margins across regions and model families.

ASSUMPTIONS (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline GPU cost per hour (amortized infra + power + infra ops) used in mock: NA=$3.10/hr, EU=$3.40/hr, APAC=$3.70/hr.
- Serving runtime config: quantized 4-bit execution for medium models; 8-bit path for large families.
- Baseline throughput metrics measured from prod traces: median tokens/request = 48, 90th = 312, mean = 85.
- Billing unit for PPK: USD per 1000 tokens.

REGIONAL PPK SLICES (mocked):
region,model_family,median_tokens,90th_tokens,ppk_median_usd,ppk_90th_usd,cost_uplift_90th_vs_median
NA,Llama-13B-q4,48,290,0.012,0.038,3.17x
EU,Llama-13B-q4,46,310,0.013,0.041,3.15x
APAC,Llama-13B-q4,52,330,0.014,0.046,3.29x
NA,Opt-70B-INT8,60,520,0.032,0.110,3.44x
EU,Opt-70B-INT8,58,540,0.034,0.118,3.47x
APAC,Opt-70B-INT8,62,560,0.036,0.125,3.47x

Interpretation: tail (90th) requests are ~3.1-3.5x more expensive per-token than median due to longer sequences and reduced batching efficiency. For larger families the absolute PPK is higher and variance increases.

SLICED SCENARIOS (short note + estimated ppk change):
1) Burst window: 5s spike where arrival rate 10x baseline -> effective batching window decreases -> ppk increases by ~18-26% for median; tails see additional 10-15% due to preempted batching.
2) Small-req heavy traffic: 70% requests <=16 tokens -> reduces batching effectiveness because overhead dominates -> median ppk increases by ~12% but 90th improves a bit as long requests get isolated and better batched.
3) Mixed-model routing without prefix caching: cross-model cold KV cache misses inflate tail cost by 20-60% depending on cache hit rate.
4) Region-specific throughput skew (APAC peak offset): when APAC is hot and NA is cold, routing to cheaper regions possible but SLO/latency penalties mean partial routing only; net margin benefit ~3-8% after accounting egress and latency SLO adjustments.

MITIGATION PLAYBOOK (practical ops + product levers):
- Micro-caching layer (0.5-2s TTL): cache responses for tiny requests (<=32 tokens) at the edge. Expected effect: reduces median PPK for small-req-heavy customers by up to 30%. Eligibility checks: idempotent endpoints, privacy flags.
- Adaptive batching windows: dynamically increase batching window in low-latency-sensitivity tier (e.g., 50ms -> 150ms) during steady flows. Improves batching fill for median and reduces tail cost by 8-15%.
- Reserve short-GPU pool for bursts: small model pool optimized for short sequences (higher throughput, lower cold-start cost). Use for short bursty workloads; reduces spike uplift by ~12-20%.
- Prefix/KV cache pinning for conversational apps: keep KV cache hot for pinned sessions (sticky routing) to reduce repeated context recompute; reduces tail PPK for conversation-heavy customers by ~18-35%.
- Paid fast-path latency tiers: offer a 2-tier product where customers pay premium for 50ms SLO; non-premium traffic enters adaptive batching and micro-cache zones. Expected revenue/cost trade: premium customers subsidize more aggressive autoscaling.
- Routing policy: early fallback to smaller/econ model variant at 95th+ token length for non-critical requests. Adds quality check but reduces PPK on extreme tails.

QUANTITATIVE EXAMPLE (one-pager style):
Customer A (chat-widget) baseline monthly tokens=120M, mix: 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long. Baseline blended PPK observed=0.018 USD. Applying micro-cache + adaptive batching -> modeled blended PPK=0.013 USD => monthly cost savings ~ $600 (per 120M tokens) or ~28% reduction. For customers with more long-tail usage, reserve pool + prefix pinning delivers larger tail reductions.

IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP (recommendation, owner, est effort):
- Q4 spike-mitigation pilot: Micro-cache for <=32-token responses (owner: Diego Morales, effort: 3w eng + 2w infra)
- Q4 adaptive batching flags (owner: Eva Brooks, effort: 4w runtime + 2w QA)
- Q1 reserve short-GPU pool MVP (owner: Infra - Hannah Li, effort: 6w infra + 3w SRE)
- Q1 prefix pinning for sessions (owner: product - Asha Patel, effort: 4w backend + 2w UX)

PRIORITIZATION MATRIX (short):
- High impact, low effort: micro-cache for tiny responses; adaptive batching flags.
- High impact, medium effort: prefix pinning, paid fast-path tiers (requires pricing changes).
- Medium impact, high effort: reserve short-GPU pool (infra heavy).

MEASUREMENT PLAN (what to track):
- PPK by bucket (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512) pre/post toggles.
- Batch fill factor and average batching window size.
- Cache hit ratio by customer and endpoint.
- Tail latency and percent of requests routed to fallback.
- Revenue uplift from paid fast-path adoption (if launched).

PLAYBOOK SNIPPET - EXAMPLE FLAGS (for runtime engineers):
- enable_micro_cache_ttl_ms=1500 (per-customer override)
- batching_target_fill=8 tokens or batching_time_ms=120
- reserve_pool_threshold_rps=200 (spin up short-model pool)

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS:
- Privacy/regulatory: micro-caching responses at edge may conflict with retention rules for some customers; need per-customer opt-outs.
- Model-quality regressions: fallbacks to smaller variants need automatic eval gating for user-visible features.
- Billing complexity: introducing paid fast-path tiers requires billing infra changes and clear customer communication.

NEXT STEPS:
1) Run a 7-day micro-cache pilot on 10 beta customers (select 3 with short-heavy traffic, 3 with mixed, 4 control).
2) Instrument batch-fill and TTL effect metrics (dashboard card + daily job).
3) Evaluate results and prepare a short exec brief with projected margin improvement and infra cost required for reserve pool.

NOTES/REFERENCES:
- Link to sample trace extract: confluence:OPT-582 -> sample_traces/sep24.csv
- Related tickets: JIRA:OPT-3421 (batching tuning), JIRA:INFRA-1999 (reserve-pool design)

(End of workbook snapshot; this is an early draft for cross-functional review. Use the linked artifacts above for the raw traces and simulation notebooks.)
